clue.text: Shrub in brush

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a yellow-flowered shrub of heathland
second meaning: a long-handled sweeping brush

explanation.surface: A bush seems to be growing in scrubland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brush' can mean scrubby undergrowth, which makes the shrub seem to grow there; really the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a heathland plant with yellow flowers and a household sweeping implement.

clue.text: Bird dog biting a lord

indicators.note: a dog biting something holds it between its jaws, so the other letters go inside

explanation.surface: A hound snaps at an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: The bite goes in after the dog's first letter, splitting the breed name in two.
explanation.definitionFit: The bald eagle is the white-headed bird of prey that serves as the national emblem of the USA.

clue.text: Porridge, we hear, for conspirator

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken word, so the clue's word is matched by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: porridge is made from rolled oats

explanation.surface: A breakfast dish is apparently the clue to a plotter.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus Oates fabricated the 'Popish Plot' of 1678, a supposed Catholic scheme to kill Charles II.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Oates is remembered in English history as the man behind an invented plot against the king.

clue.text: Parrot beginning to mimic a sound associated with a crow

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the harsh call of a crow

explanation.surface: A talking bird starts imitating a crow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large, brightly coloured tropical American parrot.

clue.text: Are they used by upwardly mobile skiers?

definitions.text: Are they used by upwardly mobile skiers?

parts.note: surface reading: skiers who are climbing the social ladder
setter's reading: literally being carried up the mountain

explanation.surface: A question about the habits of socially ambitious skiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upwardly mobile' is the idiom for social climbers; here it means physically travelling up a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: These are cabins hauled up a mountainside on overhead wires, carrying skiers to the top of the runs.

clue.text: One may interrupt a programme popular on holiday

parts.note: commercial in the sense of having mass, money-making appeal
someone on a short holiday is on a break

explanation.surface: Something popular with holidaymakers breaks into a TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On holiday' is read as the noun for a short holiday, with 'on' just part of that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause in a television or radio broadcast for advertisements interrupts the show being watched.

clue.text: Touch Queen's favourite sheep?

parts.note: to touch something is to adjoin or border it
Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, was famously the favourite of Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: Royal affection lavished on one woolly animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen here is Elizabeth I, whose favourite courtier was the Earl of Leicester.
explanation.definitionFit: The Border Leicester is a British breed of long-wool sheep, developed in the Scottish Borders.

clue.text: Six menace bewildered former government agent

indicators.note: something bewildered is thrown into confusion, so the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A confused old spy faces six threats.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciseman was an officer who collected excise duties for the government, a post now obsolete.

clue.text: Conductor beheaded in a South American country

indicators.note: a beheaded word has lost its head, meaning its first letter is cut off

parts.note: Sir Malcolm Sargent, the English orchestral conductor

explanation.surface: A conductor executed abroad in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests electricity or a bus, but it is the musician Malcolm Sargent, who loses his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a large nation in the south of the South American continent.

clue.text: Cut up rough at first, in lean-to

indicators.note: in places the preceding letter inside the word that follows

parts.note: a lean-to is a simple shed

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter only of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone was roughed up inside an outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up rough' is an idiom for getting angry, but the definition is only 'Cut up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To shred something is to cut or tear it into thin strips.

clue.text: Recent convert? That's made clear to me

indicators.note: made in the sense of fashioned or formed, so the letters after it are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A new believer says the faith has finally been explained to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's made clear to me' reads as one natural phrase of understanding; 'made' is really the signal to rearrange the three words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A latecomer arrives after others, and someone who has only recently adopted a faith or cause has come to it late.

clue.text: Smoke good one returning in vehicle

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so these letters are read backwards
in places the preceding letters inside the word that follows

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A decent man drives back home smoking.
explanation.walkthrough: G and I are reversed to IG, which goes between the C and AR of the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoke is informal for something to smoke, and a cigar is a roll of tobacco leaf for smoking.

clue.text: Heels were broken in another place

indicators.note: a broken thing has its parts knocked out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's shoe heels snapped on a different occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means somewhere other than here, at a different location.

clue.text: Council — not all gassy, no doubt

indicators.note: not all of the words are used, signalling that only a run of letters spanning them is wanted

parts.note: the letters run from the end of gassy through no into doubt

explanation.surface: A committee meeting is long-winded, though not entirely so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gassy' in the sense of windy and talkative suits a meeting, which hides the device.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of church clergy and officials that governs church affairs.

clue.text: Locum's posting is suspect, indicates journalist

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious or not right, so the letters before it are not in the right order

explanation.surface: A reporter hints that a stand-in doctor's appointment is dodgy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip columnist is a newspaper writer who reports on the private lives of celebrities.

clue.text: Saying about Conservative in the belief one's above criticism?

definitions.note: read as 'one that is above criticism', a noun phrase

indicators.note: about means around, so the saying surrounds what follows

parts.note: a saw is an old proverb or saying

indicators.note: in places the party letter inside the word for belief

parts.note: a credo is a statement of belief
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A proverb about a Tory who believes he cannot be criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions nest: the party letter goes inside the belief word, and the saying wraps round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an idea, institution or person treated as immune from questioning or attack.

clue.text: Italian lover, in his capital, turned up at opening of Othello

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means flipped to read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Italian name for Rome, the Italian's capital

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

explanation.surface: A passionate Italian turns up at the first night of Verdi's or Shakespeare's Othello in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' refers back to the Italian, so his capital is Rome in his own language, which reversed gives AMOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Inamorato is an Italian-derived word for a male lover or sweetheart.

clue.text: To transport acts, share the driving, say

parts.note: to take something somewhere is to transport it
turns are variety acts on stage

explanation.surface: A touring show's drivers share the job of moving the performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks sharing the driving as just one example of the general idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To take turns is to alternate with others at a task, as drivers swapping at the wheel do.

clue.text: The Parisienne may be taken in by ridiculous income tax assessment!?

definitions.note: the printed exclamation mark is itself the thing defined

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it
something ridiculous is absurd and makes no sense, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: la is the French feminine for 'the'
a mark is an assessment of work

explanation.surface: An outraged Parisian woman exclaims at an absurd tax bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue ends with '!?' and the definition is the '!' itself, a cheeky way to define punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation symbol placed after an exclamation, the one printed at the end of the clue.

clue.text: Run after pass from Maradona?

definitions.note: the clue's question mark signals a first name defined by a famous bearer

parts.note: to pass away is to die
a go is a run or attempt

explanation.surface: A footballer makes a run after a pass from Maradona.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the run's letters behind the pass's. Football reading of 'pass' is the trap; it means to die.
explanation.definitionFit: Diego was the first name of Maradona, the Argentine footballer, so it is defined by example.

clue.text: Sewer, initially dry, before the wet weather

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word next to it

explanation.surface: A sewage channel is dry until the rain comes.
explanation.definitionFit: A drain is a pipe or channel that carries away waste water, as a sewer does.

clue.text: Nuts in batch seem unsavoury

indicators.note: something unsavoury is unpleasant or bad, suggesting the letters are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: Some nuts in a batch taste off.
explanation.definitionFit: Beech mast is the collective name for the small triangular nuts dropped by beech trees.

clue.text: Place to say, new, on outskirts of Eccleshall

definitions.note: evidently a slip for 'Place to stay'

parts.note: hot as in hot off the press, brand new

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Eccleshall

explanation.surface: A new place to put up on the edge of a Staffordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place to say' reads as a slip for 'Place to stay'. Eccleshall is a small market town in Staffordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is an establishment offering rooms where travellers stay overnight.

clue.text: Company in a street in Berkshire

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A firm has premises on a street somewhere in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a Berkshire town, home of a famous royal racecourse; the definition is short for 'a place in Berkshire'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a town in the English county of Berkshire, known for its royal horse-race meeting.

clue.text: Bill artist for port

parts.note: ACC is short for account, a bill
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter's invoice for a glass of fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts as the drink, but it is a harbour city; Accra is the capital of Ghana.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the coastal capital city of Ghana, with a harbour on the Gulf of Guinea.

clue.text: Vehicle, say, entering race that's written about

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so the first word sits within the second
written about suggests written round the other way, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A car is said to be entering a race that is reported on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Written about' looks like 'reported on' but signals writing the word backwards. An estate car is the British term for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is a car with an extended rear load area and a back door, a station wagon.

clue.text: Novel cricketing term for a Gothamite

parts.note: in cricket a yorker is a ball pitched right at the batsman's feet

explanation.surface: Someone coins an original cricket word for a resident of Gotham.
explanation.walkthrough: Gotham is a nickname for New York City.
explanation.definitionFit: Gotham is a long-standing nickname for New York City, so a Gothamite is someone from there.

clue.text: Louts destroyed plant

indicators.note: something destroyed is wrecked and its parts scattered, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Hooligans trampled a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is an aquatic flowering plant related to the water lily.
